rationale: JTM 5.2/55 has heels as patient subject and repeated stone impact as cause. One clear physical-result context; lemma relation remains a native-speaker question.

summary: The inherited prayer contains a Preterit dəsləglux and an Infectum səlgat. Quoting the prayer once under each relevant box documents the form contrast; it does not create a second meaning of erasure.
sligi has the heels as the affected subject, without an agent suffix. Repeated contact with stones supplies an abrasion context rather than a Detransitive of literal text deletion.
The existing Turkish etymology and syl cross-reference remain unchanged; a g-bearing surface form alone cannot settle the history of the abrasion verb.
No new Idiomatic phrases: erasing sins is already represented in the existing example; heel abrasion is a physical predicate.
Confirm that sligi is the Detransitive of this slg and specifically denotes abrasion rather than another injury; one context is supplied.
Confirm the relation of the g-bearing abrasion form to slg and the cross-referenced syl without assuming identical etymology.
